M: The city wall. Somebody has carved STRENGTH into every fifth stone.
I: Stone, thick and square. Nothing in this city was built to look pretty. Everything was built to last.
H: A cottage. The garden is mostly practice dummies.
1: The Colosseum's great gate. Carved over the arch: HERE WE TEST OURSELVES.
2: The chapel. A lantern burns in the window.
3: The library. A sign: QUIET. (Somebody has added: PLEASE.)
4: The Adventurers' Guild. A notice board, crowded with jobs.
5: The hospital. It smells of herbs and soap.
7: The store. EVERYTHING YOU NEED, MOSTLY.
8: The horse barn. Something inside is chewing very loudly.
>: East: a bridge, and beyond it the Mage kingdom.
^: North: the road to the castle.
_: South: down toward the old mines, and an overgrown garden.
C: The Colosseum. Thousands of seats, and every one of them has seen a fight.
K: The statue of Kaldor, colossal, one boot on a broken crown.
The plaque: KALDOR THE KINGBREAKER. He struck down the Mad King and saved the world from war. First of the Eight. Undying.
Its eyes are two lenses of old-world glass. They follow you round the square. They probably don't.
P: The chapel. A bell hangs in the tower, and the window glows in every colour.
B: The library. Columns, and a great book over the door.
N: The Adventurers' Guild. The notice board is crowded with jobs.
V: The hospital. Clean white walls, and a sign with a green leaf.
W: The tavern. Singing, slightly off-key, and the smell of stew.
a: The store. EVERYTHING YOU NEED, MOSTLY.
r: The horse barn. Something inside is chewing very loudly.
z: The training ground's sand, raked flat and stamped flat again.
e: A straw dummy. It has been hit so often it has started to look smug.
k: A rack of practice weapons, all wood, all chipped.
g: The paddock. The grass is shorter than it should be.
u: A cottage. Window boxes, and a practice dummy in nearly every garden.
X: An iron cage in the square. Inside, days scratched into the bars. The prisoners won't look at you.
9: Old Harrow's forge. A horde quota board is nailed over the door: 40 AXES BY MOONFALL.
0: The Gut & Gauntlet. A sign of a fist holding a tankard. From inside: singing, and a chair breaking.
J: The Hall of Kaldor. Forty portraits, one king. A sign on the door: PLEASE DO NOT MENTION THE NOSE.

objects.name: Barnaby Loudmouth
lines: HEAR YE! Welcome to Warrior City, home of the COLOSSEUM!
Fights every night. Glory every fight. Seats... mostly every seat.

questions.ask: Can you put me on the bill?
answer: At the Colosseum? Nobody new's fought there in years. They'd need a very good reason.
The last man to call out the king was Aurek. Aurek the Tall. Tallest thing in the city, after the Colosseum. The king put him down in front of everyone.
Here, the strongest rules. Aurek lost, so Aurek serves. Never complains. Never smiles. Does the job. You'll see.

questions.ask: Loudmouth? Bit on the nose, isn't it?
answer: IT'S A FAMILY NAME AND WE ARE VERY PROUD OF IT!
My nan cracked the chapel window once. Twice, counting the echo.

done: {name} leans in and spins Barnaby a tale about a giant who ran from a war and came back to face it.
BARNABY: …That's the best story I've heard in five hundred years. HEAR YE! A NEW CHAMPION FIGHTS AT THE COLOSSEUM!
You're on the bill.
cant: BARNABY: A new champion? On what grounds? Give me a story, stranger, a story!
(Someone with a way with words might talk him into it.)

lines: THE CHAMPION! In MY city! The one who sent the Warden over the banners!
Your name's on the wall. In chalk, but on the wall.

objects.name: Gert
lines: Yeah, we know. He names everything after himself.
That's Kaldor Street. So's that one. They cross. You get used to it.

answer: Gert. I sell lamps. I'm the only man here who hasn't challenged you to a fight. You're welcome.
Don't make eye contact with the Crushers. The babies. They can smell weakness.
And if you're thinking of challenging the king: don't. My great-great-great-great-great-grandfather did. He fell to the king. Everyone does.
The old law's carved in the maze, if you're that sort. Hugo knows where.

questions.ask: How do I reach the king?
answer: Get yourself billed at the Colosseum in Warrior City: Barnaby does the bills, he likes a talker. Win the fights. Read the old law in the maze. Free the cages so there's a court to witness. And get Varga to agree to witness it.
Or buy a lamp. Lamps are nice.
Couldn't tell you.
I sell lamps at the border post on Thursdays, though. Read the notices while I'm there.
Somebody ought to mark them.
Old-world horns. Older than the king. Older than anybody.
At dusk they play the jingle, then a lady says nothing further is required of you. Nicest voice in the kingdom.
Nobody knows who she is. Five hundred years, same words. You get used to it.

questions.ask: Who'd buy a lamp from a man named Gert?
answer: Everybody. Eventually. It gets dark, you see. Every single night.
You'll be back at dusk. They always come back at dusk.

done: You buy a lamp. Gert looks genuinely surprised.
GERT: …Nobody's ever bought one. Huh. I'll walk you round, then. Somebody should.
Gert joins your collection.

objects.name: Tessa
lines: Kaldorbread! The only bread allowed! Tastes of nothing, like the king likes it.

answer: He eats alone. Fourteen loaves. Never shares. Never sleeps, the guards say.
Flour. Water. And, in exactly one loaf a day, my opinion.
I have a system for choosing which.

questions.ask: Why are Durn and Haskel fighting?
answer: Day eleven, is it? I was there when it started.
Last loaf of Kaldorbread on my cart. They both reached for it. Then they both remembered nobody likes it.
Neither of them would let go first. Fierce, see. Somebody ought to remind them.

questions.ask: Your bread tastes like a wet boot.
answer: That's not me, that's the recipe. By royal decree.
…Mind you, I know exactly whose loaf my opinion's going in tomorrow.

objects.name: Pim
lines: Rumours! A penny a rumour!

answer: The king is made of iron.
…That one was a penny. The next one's two.
The king is three goats in a coat. Four pennies.
The prince will come back up out of the ground, with a giant's beard.
…I made that one up. It costs the most because it's the least true.

questions.ask: Your rumours aren't worth a penny, Pim.
answer: That's a rumour too. You owe me a penny.
Two, for the cheek.

objects.name: Kett
lines: What are you looking at? I'm fierce. I'm very fierce.
…Everyone's afraid of the king. The trick is to be afraid loudly.

answer: I can't "go red". The Fury. Every raider can. I just go… pale.
Cold-blooded, they call me.
The cage guard takes bribes. Fat ones. Don't tell him I told you.

questions.ask: Fierce? You're the colour of porridge.
answer: It's PALE fury. The rarest kind of fury.
* Kett goes a shade paler. Fiercely.

objects.name: The Cage Guard
lines: Back off. King's cages, king's prisoners.
I score their cheering at the Maximus. That one's a three. That one's a two.
You? You look like a one.

answer: People who wouldn't cheer at the Maximus. They'll cheer next time.

questions.ask: You score cheers? I'd score you a zero.
answer: There is no zero. I asked for a zero. The king said no.
You're still a one. Back off.

done: {name} counts out a heavy purse, slowly, so the guard can hear every coin.
THE CAGE GUARD: …Keys must've fallen out of my pocket. Terrible. Anyway.
THE CAGE GUARD: Gerald, by the way. Nobody ever asks. Six out of ten, that purse.
(He's very tall. You hadn't noticed till now.)
The cages swing open. The prisoners stand, shaky, and follow you at a distance. They'll be witnesses.
Kett watches the cages open, then marches over to stand with the prisoners. "Someone has to look after them." Kett joins your collection.
cant: THE CAGE GUARD: Keys cost more than you've got, stranger.
(Someone who knows money might change his mind.)

lines: Gerald. Still Gerald. Unemployed Gerald.
A lady in Millbrook told my mum I'd be famous one day. Still waiting.

objects.name: Captain Varga
lines: Stop. You. Nobody walks up to the castle.
Unless they've got a reason. And a spine.

answer: Captain Varga. Second of the horde. The king took his crown with his own two hands. That's the only honest way to get one.
Any day. The king says we're finally strong enough. I can't wait.

questions.ask: Second of the horde? So, first loser.
answer: Second is a rank. Not a result.
And you're the first in a long while to say that to my face. I'll remember both.

done: VARGA: COWARD! Swing at me! Go on!
{name} breathes in, counts four, breathes out, and doesn't move.
VARGA: …Huh. Most people swing. Fine. If you challenge the king by the old law, I'll witness it. Properly.
Captain Varga joins your collection.
cant: VARGA: You flinched. Everybody flinches. Come back calmer.
(Someone steady, who won't rise to her, might earn her respect.)

objects.name: Little Brunna
lines: RAAAH.
(A toddler in tiny armour headbutts your shin. It genuinely hurts.)

answer: RAAAH.

questions.ask: Shouldn't you be having a nap?
answer: RAAAH.
* Brunna headbutts your other shin. Now they match.

done: You let Little Brunna headbutt you over. You go down dramatically.
LITTLE BRUNNA: RAAAAAH!
(It's a Tuesday. She bites you as well.)
She decides you're her friend now. Little Brunna joins your collection.

lines: A street sign with two arms. One reads KALDOR STREET.
The other reads KALDOR STREET. They point different ways.
The Crier's board: VICTORIES OF THE KING: see previous notice.
The previous notice: see previous notice.
Underneath, in pencil: "riveting."
KALDOR'S LITTLE CRUSHERS PLAYPEN. This way. No biting.
Smaller, underneath: Biting is for Tuesdays.
Wedged behind a rain barrel, out of the horde's sight: a Heart Piece.
Somebody in this town still hides good things.

objects.name: Durn
lines: He looked at my axe.
HASKEL: I looked AT it. Not FOR it. There's a difference!
DURN: Day eleven. I'm not stopping first.

questions.ask: Is this about the last Kaldorbread?
answer: DURN: …
HASKEL: …
DURN: Nobody even likes Kaldorbread.
HASKEL: It tastes of nothing. Like the king likes it.
DURN: Eleven days.
HASKEL: Drink?
DURN: Drink.
then: Durn and Haskel let go of each other, stare at their fists for a while, and wander off east toward the city, arm in arm, for a drink.

questions.ask: You two fight like a pair of wet socks.
answer: DURN: Wet socks.
HASKEL: My socks are bone dry, thank you very much.
DURN: …Mine aren't. Don't tell anyone.

objects.name: Haskel
lines: I don't remember why we started. That's not the point.
The point is he started it.
DURN: YOU started it!

answer: Because then he'd have stopped second. And I'd have stopped first. Do you see?
DURN: HE SEES. EVERYONE SEES.
Odd Bett says nobody, every day, at the same odds. Sister Hild says the scarf.
Little Brunna says she is. She headbutted us both on day four. She might be right.
I did lose to Brunna. Day four. We don't talk about day four.
DURN: HE CRIED.
HASKEL: I HAD SOMETHING IN MY EYE. IT WAS BRUNNA.

objects.name: Odd Bett
lines: Bets! Bets on the brawl! Odds on Durn: same as yesterday. Odds on Haskel: also same as yesterday.
Kaldor coins only. No markers, no IOUs, no 'I'll owe you a headbutt'.
Fight's off. Eleven days of the best odds in the kingdom, and they go for a DRINK.
Worst day of my life. Don't talk to me.

questions.ask: Who bets on a fight that never ends?
answer: Everybody. That's the beauty. Nobody wins, nobody loses, the coins just go round and round, through me.
Pim sells the rumours, I sell the odds. Between us we're the whole economy of Kaldor Street. Both of them.
Durn's been eating Tessa's Kaldorbread. Haskel hasn't. Make of that what you will.
Tessa says it tastes of nothing. I say nothing is very filling if you eat enough of it.
My odds are the same every day. That's called reliable, love.
For being rude, odds on you: long. Very long. You'd need a ladder.

objects.name: Sister Hild
lines: Day eleven. I've brought a stool, a bucket, and a lot of yarn.
Whoever drops first, I'll patch him up. Neither of them has dropped. I've knitted a scarf.
They've gone for a drink. Together. Eleven days, and it was the bread.
I'll finish the scarf anyway. It's a very long scarf now.

answer: Day one was a scarf. Day five, mittens. Day nine, a jumper for Hamm's boulder. Pebble gets cold.
If the brawl goes on to day thirty, I'll have done the whole street.

questions.ask: Do you patch up anyone else?
answer: Gudrun's hands, when the cage bars give her blisters. Rumm's belly, when he drums it raw.
The medic up at the castle sends folk down to me. He's lovely. He isn't a medic.
The bucket is for whoever needs it. Today, perhaps, that's whoever's been rude to a nun.
* She keeps knitting. The needles click in a way that feels pointed.

objects.name: Drum-warden Tuk
lines: BOOM. Curfew patrol. BOOM. Keep moving. BOOM.
We march in step. Tok is out of step. Tok has always been out of step.

questions.ask: What does the patrol actually do?
answer: Curfew. We walk. We BOOM. People go inside.
Nobody's been out after curfew in sixty years. The BOOM is very effective.

questions.ask: You're the one out of step.
answer: …No.
* BOOM. He checks his feet. BOOM. He checks Tok's feet. BOOM. He looks worried.

objects.name: Drum-warden Tok
lines: BOOM. …BOOM.
I'm in step. Tuk's out of step. Rumm hasn't got a drum. Some patrol.

questions.ask: Why only one boom at a time?
answer: Saving the second one. You never know when you'll need a second boom.
Tuk wastes his. Booms everywhere. Show-off.

questions.ask: Is that a drum or a bucket?
answer: It is a drum.
…It was a bucket. Sister Hild lent it. Don't tell Tuk.

objects.name: Drum-warden Rumm
lines: *slap* *slap*
Lost my drum. Belly works fine. Don't tell the captain.
*slap*

answer: Bet it on Durn. Day two. Odd Bett has it now. She uses it as a stool.
*slap* Belly's lighter to carry anyway.
*slap*
It's an instrument. Everything's an instrument if you're brave enough. *slap* *slap*

objects.name: Old Gudrun
lines: Ninety-one. Ninety-two. Don't interrupt.
Chin-ups on the cage bars. The bars are the only thing in this town that don't wobble.
Ninety-three. When I was a girl I did these on the old king's gate. Ninety-four.

questions.ask: How did you get so strong?
answer: Every day. Little bit. Never skipped. That's all it is, and nobody believes me.
Strength's not a gift, dear. It's a habit you didn't put down. Ninety-five.

questions.ask: What was the old king like?
answer: Hale. Kind man. Open hand. Let children swing on his gate. I was one of them.
Kaldor took the gate down. I took up the cage bars. Ninety-six.

questions.ask: Bet you can't do a hundred.
answer: Ninety-seven. Ninety-eight. Ninety-nine. One hundred.
One hundred and one. Now you do one, dear. Go on. I'll wait.

objects.name: Hamm
lines: Training. Carrying the boulder. Six years now.
Same boulder. I named him Pebble. Pebble isn't a pebble. That's the joke. I don't get many visitors.

answer: The horde said, 'carry something heavy till you're strong.' Didn't say when to stop. So I haven't.
Pebble and I have seen the whole street. Both Kaldor Streets. He likes the bakery best. Tessa waves.

questions.ask: Pebble's your only friend, isn't he?
answer: …Pebble's a very good friend. Never interrupts. Never leaves.
* Hamm hugs the boulder a little tighter. The boulder, being a boulder, says nothing kind back.

objects.name: Fliss
lines: Kaldor's Sweat! Genuine sweat of the king! Tiny bottles! Makes you strong!
…It's water. It's water from the well. But it's Kaldor's Well, so technically.

answer: Raiders before a fight. Sorrel buys six. She says it's for her knees.
Mott tried to tax it. I gave him a bottle. He's stronger now. Technically.

questions.ask: I can see the bucket you're filling it from.
answer: That's a different bucket. A royal bucket.
…Two for one. Please. Don't tell Mott.

objects.name: Brakka
lines: Furs. Best furs in Kaldorhold. Twenty push-ups and we'll talk.
No push-ups, no furs. I don't make the rules. Well. I made this one. I like it.

questions.ask: Where do the furs come from?
answer: North. Up past the Frost Ward. My cousins trap. I sell. I make you do push-ups.
Elder Skadi says the old Kaldari wore wolves. I say wolves wore them first.

questions.ask: Twenty push-ups? I'll pass on fleas.
answer: Fleas! These furs are clean! I washed them in Fliss's well. Kaldor's Well.
Sixty push-ups now. Price went up. For you.

objects.name: Snik
lines: Sharpening! Axes, swords, spoons, bread, a cat's patience. I sharpen anything.
Brought me a pillow once. Took a week. Very pointy pillow now.

answer: Hroth. Brings the same axe every week. It's sharp. He just likes the chat.
Ansel Chisk brings his chisels. Says Kaldor's nose keeps breaking them. Very hard nose.
Ooh. I'll try. Leave them overnight.
* He holds out his hand for your wits. He's waiting.
…No? Pointy pillow, then. Half price.

objects.name: Ansel Chisk
lines: The king wants another statue. I've done Kaldor standing. Kaldor striding. Kaldor looking at Kaldor.
Kaldor… sitting? Kaldor… thinking? Does he think? I can't ask. You can't ask.

answer: Two hundred and twelve. All Kaldor. Some are the same statue facing the other way.
There's a pigeon on the big one I've grown fond of. It's the only thing in this city not owned by the king.

questions.ask: What happened to the old statues?
answer: Under us. He built Kaldorhold on top of the old city. Old kings, old gods. Buried, standing up.
Dig a well and you hit somebody's marble foot. Fliss's well has a whole marble toe at the bottom.

questions.ask: Your Kaldors all have the same face.
answer: He only has the one face!
…Shh. If he hears 'same face' I'll be doing Kaldor-hitting-a-sculptor next. From life.

objects.name: Mott
lines: Tax collector. Not coin. Fights. Everybody here owes the king fights.
You, for example. Visitor. You owe nothing yet. I've opened a page for you, though. Just in case.

questions.ask: What happens if you don't pay?
answer: The Kaldorium Maximus. Or the fighters' cells first. Then the Maximus.
Joss's whole camp owed a tithe. They sent Joss. He writes about clouds. I felt bad. I wrote it down anyway.
Paid? Nobody gets paid. The king pays in honour.
I've got a page for honour. It's empty. Don't tell anyone.

questions.ask: Tax collector? Did your mum know?
answer: She did. She owes three fights. I've got her page right here.
* He writes something on your page. Underlines it twice.

objects.name: Tib
lines: Fight club. Behind the houses. Rule one: tell everyone about fight club.
Rule two: no crying. Rule three: Brunna's not allowed. She bites.

answer: Brunna. She bites. Brunna's not allowed. Brunna keeps coming.
Next week we're doing teams. It's me and a dog against Brunna. I think it's even.

questions.ask: Fight club's just you hitting a fence.
answer: The fence hit me first.
Rule four: no being mean. I just made it. You're out.

lines: Behind the Hall of Kaldor, in a crate marked RETURNS: a Heart Piece.
Somebody tried to sell it at the bazaar. Nobody could do enough push-ups.
Under the arena's outer stairs, where the children hide their wooden swords: a Heart Piece.

objects.name: Joss
lines: I'm here for the tithe. From the camps. My mum knitted me armour.
It's wool. It's very thick wool. I'm a poet, really. I write about clouds.

answer: Yes. Very.
But I wrote a poem about it, and the poem's less scared than me, so I read it before I go out.
It's called 'Cloud, Heading Into a Storm, Being Brave About It'. It's quite long.

questions.ask: Wool armour? You'll lose to a moth.
answer: …Mum said that about the moths too.
I'm going to write a poem about you. It's going to be about a very small, very grey cloud.
Nobody's going to like it. That's the point.

objects.name: Edda
lines: Tithe fighter. Never held an axe. I held a goose once. It went badly.
They say you do the ladder. Beat Hroth and the tithe might change. That's what people whisper.

answer: It went for my ankles. I went for the hills. The goose won the hills.
My village said, 'Edda's brave, she fought a goose.' Next thing I'm the tithe.
Joss heard it from a guard. The guard heard it from Tova. Tova hears everything.
If somebody beats Hroth, the ladder changes. Maybe the tithe too. Maybe it's just a nice thing people say in cells.

questions.ask: Bet the goose would win this too.
answer: …It would. Geese don't fear anyone.
I'll tell it you said hello. It'll find you.
